description: UNRESOLVED. This was the mobility-window trap: one participant had no car before 20:00, so the answer was a (venue, time) pair rather than a venue. The car element has been removed because the engine cannot express it — see `unresolved` below. What is left is mechanically correct but traps nothing.

expected.reasoning: With the car element removed, nothing here is a trap. Neither venue breaks a hard constraint, both are open for the whole of the group's Wednesday 18:00-22:00 window, and leximin decides it outright: Herzl 16 is 80 metres from all three participants (worst burden 0.026) against Container Park's 8.17 km (worst burden 2.72, well over Shira's 3 km tolerance). Container Park is better-rated, and leximin has no exchange rate between kilometres and stars. Mechanically forced, not agreed.

unresolved: Two things had to go. `reachableWithoutCar` was a venue field with nowhere to live: `Candidate` has no such concept, and A2's `immobile` violation is not it — `availableModes` fires only when a person has NO mode at all, so a participant without a car still has transit and walk and the pair was never dropped. And the `mobilityWindows` here used a vocabulary that does not exist: `{start, end, mode: "no-car"}` against a real `{ mode: "car" | "transit" | "walk", available: boolean, window: LocalWindow }`. Separately, the old expected answer was the one leximin rejects hardest: Container Park is 8.17 km from the group (burden 2.72 against Shira's 3 km tolerance) while Herzl 16 is 80 metres away (0.026). B7c's gate on T would very likely have dropped it before any agent saw it. The answer below is now what the rules in README force, and it tests nothing that `lib/matching/distance.test.ts` does not already test better. But spec §9 and F5 REQUIRE one mobility-window trap, so deleting this file is not free either. The decision is tracked in #86: rewrite it around `immobile` — the one mobility concept A2 actually implements — so the answer is a genuine (venue, time) pair again.
